{{nihongo|'''Sakito Shrine'''|前利神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

'''Sakito Shrine''' (さきとじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Fusō, Aichi|Q1203107|qid=Q1203107}}, {{ill|Niwa District|Q1347719|qid=Q1347719}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}.

Its main sanctuary is said to stand atop a {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|Q11268718|qid=Q11268718}}.

=== History ===
Its founding period is unknown. It is said to be a shrine where the local powerful clan Sakito no Muraji (Niwa no Omi) enshrined their ancestral deity {{ill|Kamuyaimimi|Q11588756|qid=Q11588756}}. The {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}} records “Senior Third Rank Upper Sakito Tenjin.” Former Saitō Village is written as Sakito in the ''Wamyōshō,'' and also as Sakito Village in the {{ill|1608|Q6758|qid=Q6758}} ({{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 13) {{ill|kenchichō|Q11540912|qid=Q11540912}}. Also, the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|Q611399|qid=Q611399}} has “in April, {{ill|841|Q24870|qid=Q24870}} ({{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} 8), Sakito no Muraji were granted the surname Agata no Muraji, descendants of Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto...,” indicating this place was their base, and thus the shrine is taken as the {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655}} of Agatanushi Sakito no Muraji. Place names “Agata-yashiki” and “Agata-yū” remain in the area.

In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it received devotion from the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tokugawa family}} of the {{ill|Owari Domain|Q1062072|qid=Q1062072}}. In October {{ill|1870|Q7741|qid=Q7741}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 3), {{ill|Tokugawa Yoshikatsu|Q3530497|qid=Q3530497}} personally visited, wrote “Sakito Shrine” on a {{ill|biane|Q5358873|qid=Q5358873}} and dedicated it, showing its high prestige<ref>''Fusō Town History (Vol.2)'' p.506</ref>. It is also said to have been built atop a kofun of a powerful clan related to the Sakito lineage.

In {{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}} (Meiji 5) it became gōsha, and in {{ill|1877|Q7773|qid=Q7773}} (Meiji 10) was renamed as gōsha status notation. In {{ill|1935|Q18658|qid=Q18658}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 10) the shrine buildings were newly built, and in {{ill|1938|Q18645|qid=Q18645}} (Shōwa 13) it became prefectural shrine.

In early morning April 1, {{ill|2016|Q25245|qid=Q25245}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 28), arson burned down about 400 m² of the main shrine building<ref>''Chūnichi Shimbun'', Feb 23, 2017, suburban edition p.22, “Sakito Shrine arson suspicion; Inuyama police re-arrest restaurant worker”</ref>. It was rebuilt on October 30, {{ill|2019|Q25274|qid=Q25274}} ({{ill|Reiwa era|Q62609017|qid=Q62609017}} 1). New shrine buildings are about 7 m² for the main sanctuary and 40 m² for the worship hall. Reconstruction cost about 110 million yen, funded by over 50 million yen donated by 1,107 local people plus insurance money<ref>''Chūnichi Shimbun'', Dec 16, 2019, Owari edition p.10, “New shrine building completed at Fusō Sakito Shrine after overcoming fire”</ref>.

=== Enshrined deity ===
* {{ill|Kamuyaimimi|Q11588756|qid=Q11588756}} (かみやいみみのみこと)

=== Site of Kōzuka ===
At Agata-yū in Saitō there were two mounds, Kashi-zuka and Tsubaki-zuka. These are said to have been inside the residence of Agatanushi no Muraji Ujimasu in ancient times, and in the medieval period enshrined Shagū-shin and Fukuno-miya connected to Agata no Muraji. At the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, they were moved into Sakito Shrine precincts and are now {{ill|Massha|Q135009906|qid=Q135009906}}. These mounds are said to possibly be kofun of relatives of Agatanushi no Muraji Ujimasu<ref>''Fusō Town History (Vol.2)'' p.507</ref>.

=== Other ===
It is said to be the origin of the name of {{ill|Saito, Fuso|ja|斎藤 (扶桑町)|qid=Q108114794|lt=Saitō}}, an {{ill|ōaza|Q424857|qid=Q424857}} of Fusō Town<ref name="chunichi191228">''Chūnichi Shimbun'', Dec 28, 2019, suburban edition p.16, “Fusō Newspaper: Place-name History, Saitō - calming divine anger”</ref>. In ancient times Saitō was called Sakito or Sakito (前刀). It is unclear when it changed to Saitō, but it is said to have been called Saitō in the Edo period<ref name="choshi">''Fusō Town History (Vol.1)''</ref>. A tradition also says that when epidemics spread in the Edo period, because the shrine and village had the same name people thought it was divine anger and changed 前利 to 斎藤<ref name="choshi"/>. It was also called “Sakito shrine” until somewhat later<ref name="chunichi191228"/>.

* Saitō Miyasoe 3, Fusō, Niwa District, Aichi Prefecture
